mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the current month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-inflation period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs indicates labor market strength that supports corporate earnings optimism, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the correlation between PAYEMS strength and SPX 20-day returns remains below 0.3 in absolute value.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 anticipates a policy tightening response that reduces future growth prospects, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During such inflation spikes, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests weakening manufacturing momentum that reduces earnings expectations, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the average 60-day forward return during INDPRO contractions is not significantly lower than during expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining residential mortgage applications (not available in the catalog) would imply tightening credit conditions, but since HOUST is available, we proxy: a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,600 suggests reduced building activity and a negative 20-day SPX return expectation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns during HOUST declines are not statistically lower than during stable periods (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.8% signals tight labor markets that boost investor confidence, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Over 6 months, the average 20-day return during UNRATE < 3.8 is not higher than during UNRATE ≥ 3.8 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below their 2023 Q4 averages creates a dual headwind that depresses earnings expectations, producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During such dual declines, the 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 60-day average of the past 2 years (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be negative as investors anticipate higher interest rates and slower growth.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS rising trend AND UNRATE falling trend
failure_condition: In the identified regime, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative across 5 non-overlapping windows (average p > 0.1).
